chunks: A group, from Sahl, from Muhammad, from his father, from Abu Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the statement of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'By the sun and its brilliance' (91:1). He said: The sun is the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — through him God, Mighty and Majestic, clarified for the people their religion.

He (the narrator) said: I then said (what about) 'And the moon when it follows it' (91:2)? He said: That is the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who followed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and emitted knowledge into him by a radiant infusion.

He (the narrator) said: I said (what about) 'And the night when it covers it' (91:4)? He said: That refers to the imams of injustice who usurped authority to the exclusion of the family of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and they sat in a position which the family of the Messenger were more deserving of than them. Thus they veiled the religion of God with injustice and tyranny, and God recorded their deed and said: 'And the night when it covers it' (91:4).

He (the narrator) said: I said (what about) 'And the day when it reveals its clarity' (91:3)? He said: That is the Imam from the descendants of Fatima (peace be upon her) — when asked about the religion of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) he clarifies it for whoever asks him. And so God, Mighty and Majestic, referred to this in His statement, saying: 'And the day when it reveals its clarity' (91:3).

key_terms.أَئِمَّةُ الْجَوْرِ: Imams of injustice — term used in Shia tradition for the illegitimate caliphs
key_terms.اللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا: Quran 91:4 — 'The night when it covers it'; interpreted as the unjust rulers
key_terms.النَّهَارِ إِذَا جَلَّاهَا: Quran 91:3 — 'The day when it reveals its clarity'; interpreted as the Imams from Fatima's progeny
key_terms.الْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَاهَا: Quran 91:2 — 'The moon when it follows the sun'; interpreted as Imam Ali (AS)
key_terms.نَفَثَهُ بِالْعِلْمِ نَفْثاً: He emitted/imparted knowledge by a radiant infusion — metaphor for the Prophet transmitting divine knowledge to Imam Ali
key_terms.وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا: Quran 91:1 — 'By the sun and its brilliance'; interpreted as the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of Surah al-Shams according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an esoteric (ta'wil) interpretation of Surah al-Shams (91) by Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) in response to a disciple's questions. The cosmological imagery of the surah — sun, moon, night, and day — is decoded as referring to the Imamate: the Prophet (SAWW) is the sun who illuminates religion, Imam Ali (AS) is the moon who follows and reflects that light, the unjust usurpers are the night that veils the truth, and the Imams from Fatima's lineage are the day that reveals and clarifies the religion. This form of Quranic commentary, common in al-Kafi, grounds Shia theological claims about legitimate authority in the direct word of God.
